Regulation in Europe: EU AI Act and the EU Data Act
A key aspect of the EUâs approach to AI is a focus on regulation. The EU has advanced regulation significantly in key areas, including the introduction of comprehensive legislation governing AI. Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the EU AI Act) establishes a harmonized framework that categorizes AI systems into prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk and minimal-risk, with corresponding regulatory obligations. High-risk AI systems encompass applications critical to the safety of essential infrastructures, such as data centers. For example, AI systems used to monitor water pressure or manage fire alarm controls in cloud-computing centers are classified as high-risk and must comply with stringent regulatory requirements. In contrast, AI systems developed exclusively for cybersecurity purposes may not fall within the high-risk classification. Organizations deploying high-risk AI systems must conduct rigorous risk assessments, adhere to strict safety standards and implement robust data governance measures to ensure the security and reliability of AI in critical sectors. evidence.excerpt:
/PRNewswire/ -- SWI Compute today emerged from stealth to build and operate NVIDIA AI factories, launching first in Europe. The global AI infrastructure company is backed by 3.6 gigawatts of power capacity that SWI Group has spent six years securing across Europe and the US. The new company of Euronext Amsterdam-listed SWI Group became a Preferred NVIDIA Cloud Partner in August, ordered approximately $1 billion of NVIDIA systems and has finalized contracts with its first customers. SWI Compute will deploy globally, with the strongest presence and deployments in Europe. Its first large-scale AI factory in the UK starts with 30 MW, close to 7,000 Rubin GPUs and 3,500 Vera CPUs in NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, expected to come online by the end of 2027. Connected by NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, these 30 MW are the initial phase of a UK campus planned to grow to 530 MW, and the first step towards 2.3 GW of NVIDIA AI factory capacity by 2029.
"Energy availability represents the primary bottleneck facing European AI infrastructure. Having spent six years acquiring grid access, SWI Group is now deploying these power resources into dedicated NVIDIA AI factories through SWI Compute. Just two months after joining the NVIDIA Cloud Partner program, our team secured approximately $1 billion in advanced hardware orders and executed initial client contracts. The market continues to surpass available capacity, and we are rapidly expanding our footprint to fulfill this requirement," said
Europe has the researchers, the founders and the enterprises to build frontier AI. Much of that building has happened on capacity outside Europe, and the capacity that exists has been committed first to global hyperscalers and frontier labs, the buyers able to sign multi-year contracts at scale. The companies with the most urgent need, AI natives with frontier ambitions and startup balance sheets, have the hardest time securing it.

/PRNewswire/ -- SWI Compute today emerged from stealth to build and operate NVIDIA AI factories, launching first in Europe. The global AI infrastructure company is backed by 3.6 gigawatts of power capacity that SWI Group has spent six years securing across Europe and the US. The new company of Euronext Amsterdam-listed SWI Group became a Preferred NVIDIA Cloud Partner in August, ordered approximately $1 billion of NVIDIA systems and has finalized contracts with its first customers. SWI Compute will deploy globally, with the strongest presence and deployments in Europe. Its first large-scale AI factory in the UK starts with 30 MW, close to 7,000 Rubin GPUs and 3,500 Vera CPUs in NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, expected to come online by the end of 2027. Connected by NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, these 30 MW are the initial phase of a UK campus planned to grow to 530 MW, and the first step towards 2.3 GW of NVIDIA AI factory capacity by 2029.
"Energy availability represents the primary bottleneck facing European AI infrastructure. Having spent six years acquiring grid access, SWI Group is now deploying these power resources into dedicated NVIDIA AI factories through SWI Compute. Just two months after joining the NVIDIA Cloud Partner program, our team secured approximately $1 billion in advanced hardware orders and executed initial client contracts. The market continues to surpass available capacity, and we are rapidly expanding our footprint to fulfill this requirement,"Â said
Europe has the researchers, the founders and the enterprises to build frontier AI. Much of that building has happened on capacity outside Europe, and the capacity that exists has been committed first to global hyperscalers and frontier labs, the buyers able to sign multi-year contracts at scale. The companies with the most urgent need, AI natives with frontier ambitions and startup balance sheets, have the hardest time securing it.

best AI GPU for memory intensive workloads
, match your hardware to actual workload requirements rather than chasing specs. You should profile your models, find the bottlenecks and then pick the GPU to solve your real problems. Various types of GPUs are used within various organizations: H100 is used by organizations in full production, MI300X is used by organizations to serve inferences, and Gaudi3 is used by organizations in research clusters. NVIDIA H100 offers the best overall performance with mature software support. AMD MI300X works better for models over 100B parameters due to its 192GB memory. Intel Gaudi3 provides good value at half the cost if you have engineering resources for optimization.
